prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1263; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for a left-turn collision at an intersection. Insured states the oncoming vehicle was approaching at speed when they began their turn. Police report requested. No citations were noted on the scene summary.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant reports pain in the right knee after the airbag deployed and the door frame struck the leg. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and indicated they are handling the matter personally. Advised claimant of the claims process and requested medical records.

Entry 3: Received photos of both vehicles from the insured and the claimant. Damage to the insured's front bumper and left headlamp is consistent with a broadside impact on the claimant's driver side. Scene diagram from the police report shows both vehicles stopped in the intersection. Liability appears to lean toward the insured pending witness statements.

Entry 4: Claimant provided an initial urgent care note describing a knee sprain with swelling and limited range of motion. Follow-up with an orthopedic provider has been recommended by the treating physician. Requested itemized bills and confirmed the claimant's health insurance information for coordination of benefits.

Entry 5: Reviewed the independent witness statement, which supports the claimant's account that the insured turned in front of the approaching vehicle. Set reserves for property damage and bodily injury based on current medical documentation. Scheduled a follow-up call with the claimant in two weeks to check treatment progress and any further records.
